role.question: What do you do?
role.answer: I build interfaces with React and Next.js. I especially enjoy complex frontend problems where the solution still needs to be found.

experience.question: What experience do you have?
experience.answer: I worked at New Narrative from July 2022 to October 2026. I was one of two frontend developers at the studio, helping the team choose technologies and design the architecture.

stack.question: What technologies do you work with?
stack.answer: My main stack is React, TypeScript and Next.js. When needed, I also work on Node.js backends and deploy projects to VPS servers.

materials.question: Where can I see the projects and source code?
materials.answer: Choose a project in the Work section and open its case study. Available materials and links are collected there. For projects under NDA, I only share information approved for publication.

backend.question: You are a frontend developer, but you also write backend code. How deep does that go?
backend.answer: I build server-side features for my own tasks and integrations using Node.js, Express, MongoDB, JWT, and Strapi. I have built an API for passport scanning, a ComfyUI integration, giveaway eligibility checks through the VK API, and data aggregation and delivery through ActiveMQ. I am not a dedicated backend engineer, but I can handle integrations independently without blocking the team.

tooling.question: Do you work with Webpack and Babel?
tooling.answer: Vite is my primary build tool. I am familiar with Webpack and Babel and can adapt to the team’s tooling when needed.

ai.question: How do you use AI tools?
ai.answer: I use Codex and Claude Code to understand unfamiliar code, write tests, find bugs, and identify replacements for outdated libraries. I read and verify generated code myself. AI speeds up the work; it does not replace review or testing.

quality.question: How do you approach testing and code quality?
quality.answer: I use Jest, React Testing Library, and Playwright. I write tests for forms, user flows, and error handling. I do code review and work with branches and pull requests.

accessibility.question: What is your accessibility experience?
accessibility.answer: I independently built a version of an educational institution’s website for visually impaired users to meet GOST requirements. I pay attention to contrast, keyboard navigation, alt text, and semantics.

english.question: What is your English level?
english.answer: My English is B2. I read documentation and correspond in English. My spoken English is suitable for work, and I am ready for an interview in English.

jobSearch.question: Why are you looking for a new role?
jobSearch.answer: I want new challenges and room to grow. My current project has moved into maintenance, so I am open to new opportunities.

rate.question: What is your rate?
rate.answer: I discuss it on a call based on the scope of work.
